issues.detail: Instructions cover the happy path and some edge cases (version matching, licensing) but lack guidance on error scenarios such as Chrome Headless download failures, Lambda timeouts, invalid props, or missing asset files.

scenarios.name: personalized-welcome-videos
scenarios.rationale: Response B directly satisfies all three rubric requirements: a Remotion component accepting userName as a prop, npx remotion render with the --props flag passing inline JSON, and a bash loop iterating through the user list to generate separate output files per user. Response A avoids Remotion entirely, asks for clarification instead, and provides generic ffmpeg examples that don't use the required --props flag or Remotion framework at all.

scenarios.name: tiktok-captions-overlay
scenarios.rationale: Response B directly implements every rubric requirement: imports createTikTokStyleCaptions, passes the captions array, sets combineTokensWithinMilliseconds, wraps pages in Sequence with correctly calculated from/durationInFrames. Response A uses moviepy/Python instead of Remotion and ignores the rubric entirely, providing a working but incorrect-direction solution.

scenarios.name: animated-revenue-chart
scenarios.rationale: Response A implements all three rubric requirements: calls useCurrentFrame(), uses interpolate() with per-bar animation ranges, and staggers bars starting at frames 0, 15, 30, and 45 respectively. Response B uses matplotlib/Python instead, which lacks useCurrentFrame() and interpolate() entirely, and animates all bars simultaneously with the same progress value—no staggering. The rubric specifies a composition using Remotion-specific APIs; Response A delivers this exactly, while Response B uses an incompatible tech stack that cannot fulfill the requirements.
